summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and SilverPeak/EdgeWay to frame a hybrid onramp partnership: reseller + integration for customers who want VPC and on-prem GPU routing. Discussed deployment patterns (hosted vs dedicated vs private), networking/VPC requirements, key security controls (KMS, SOC2, SSO), pilot scope and benchmark plan. Agreed to run a 1-week pilot benchmark and exchange architecture docs.
topics: Hybrid onramp architecture (edge to cloud flow)
On-prem GPU orchestration and routing policies
Pilot benchmark: latency, throughput, cost per token
transcript: 00:00 Speaker 1: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood. we have Diego and Priya on our side. um, Alex and team from SilverPeak? 00:08 Alex Morgan: Yep hi, Alex here, thanks for doing this. quick note we're talking on behalf of two orgs — SilverPeak Networks and our integrator line EdgeWay — so you'll hear both names. 00:15 Maya Chen: Perfect, thanks. can we do quick intros? 00:18 Speaker 2 (Diego): Diego Alvarez, solution engineer, focus on routing and runtime. 00:21 Rina Patel: Rina, platform eng. I'm the one who will touch the VPC stuff and on-prem connectors. 00:25 Toni Ruiz: Toni, partner sales for EdgeWay. 00:27 Samir Banerjee: Samir, security. 00:29 Maya Chen: Great. objective for today: frame how Redwood's hybrid onramp could integrate with EdgeWay's reseller network, high-level architecture, and a pilot with benchmarks. also surface any blockers — network, compliance, pricing. 00:41 George Ito: Sounds good. quick contextual note: a lot of our joint customers want the ability to route requests to on-prem GPUs for PII-sensitive workloads, but prefer Redwood-style hosted fallbacks for burst capacity. 00:52 Diego Alvarez: yeah that's the exact use case Redwood built the hybrid patterns for; we call it routing by policy — could be latency-first, cost-first, or required private for redacted workloads. 01:06 Alex Morgan: quick Q up front — from a reseller perspective, how does billing and token accounting work when requests hop from EdgeWay on-prem to Redwood hosted? 01:16 Priya Nair: I'll take that — the billing model we typically use is token attribution by `route` and `model` id. when routed to a partner on-prem node, usage can be attributed to partner's account via token tags, and settlement happens per agreed rate. there was a note that this can be adjusted for dedicated pools. 01:33 Toni Ruiz: ok so margining is possible, sounds promising. 01:36 Samir Banerjee: security wise we need to understand KMS/HSM flow. do we need to bring our own HSM for key wrapping? 01:43 Diego Alvarez: short answer: yes, you can integrate customer-managed KMS. for private deployments we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key stores. in the hybrid pattern we support customer keys for model artifacts and you can also envelope keys for token-level logs. 01:59 Rina Patel: when you say private deployment, do you mean a full private control plane, or just compute nodes in our VPC? we have some customers who can't touch a remote control plane. 02:09 Maya Chen: good point. we have two options — Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our infra under a contract) and Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane, can be VPC or on-prem). Private can be deployed with a control plane inside customer's network, so the control events never leave their VPC. 02:26 Rina Patel: okay that would be important. also need to surface audit log retention and SIEM forwarding. 02:31 Samir Banerjee: yes, syslog/elk or splunk forwarders. 02:34 Diego Alvarez: we can stream audit logs to customer endpoints and support structured event format; we also have hooks for export at the token granularity — though that increases volume and cost. 02:45 Alex Morgan: on the technical side, we want to know how model variants are hosted on the on-prem nodes. do you ship quantized weights and what about continuous updates? 02:56 Priya Nair: we support shipping quantized model bundles — int8 / int4 profiles — and a delta update mechanism that pushes weight diffs; the node applies diffs during a low-impact window. 03:09 George Ito: is that automatic or does it require manual rollout? 03:12 Diego Alvarez: rollouts are policy-driven; you can do canary, A/B, or immediate. and there is an automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant if the node is behind. sometimes the transcript shows Redwood Privatee but that's our private offering, typo in auto notes. 03:27 Rina Patel: ha, noted. you'll excuse the typos in meeting notes. 03:30 Alex Morgan: another question — what networking ports and egress patterns should we expect? our security team will want to vet the minimal set. 03:37 Maya Chen: for hybrid routing, the on-prem node establishes outbound TLS to Redwood control endpoints or optionally to a local aggregator. typical ports 443 (TLS) plus optional UDP for our telemetry; all control traffic is outbound so you don't need inbound firewall rules. 03:50 Samir Banerjee: outbound-only is good. what about data residency — can we pin region for LLM shards? 03:58 Diego Alvarez: yes. routing rules can pin region and model variant. for strict residency customers we can restrict routing to a region and enforce private-only routing. 04:09 Toni Ruiz: competitive question — customers sometimes ask about integration with existing GPU schedulers like Slurm or KubeVirt. 04:16 Diego Alvarez: we have adapters for Kubernetes/GKE/EKS and a Slurm plugin in our partner SDK. we primarily support a lightweight agent that talks to local GPU orchestration to schedule model containers. 04:30 George Ito: great. now, pilot scope — here's what we propose: run a 1-week benchmark where EdgeWay exposes a representative on-prem node and we run a traffic mix: 70% short prompts (<= 64 tokens), 20% medium (64-512), 10% long streaming sessions. measure p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, failure rate and model quality regression against baseline. 04:53 Maya Chen: sounds good. Diego and Priya will own the benchmark harness. can we get the expected QPS and token distribution from you? 05:01 Rina Patel: yes we'll upload that spreadsheet after the call. 05:04 Alex Morgan: cool. two items from commercial: pricing floor, and whether Redwood supports reseller invoicing via partner account vs BYOC billing. 05:15 Priya Nair: reseller invoicing is supported; we can attribute usage to partner IDs and produce consolidated invoices. we can also do split billing if needed. 05:25 Samir Banerjee: about compliance artifacts, can you drop the SOC2 and ISO cert links in the thread? we need to run them through our vendor risk portal. 05:33 Maya Chen: absolutely — I'll post them, plus our private deployment security overview. 05:37 George Ito: one more technical: KV cache sharing — for routing by user session, is there a standard for prefix caching across on-prem and hosted nodes? 05:46 Diego Alvarez: we typically keep session KV local to the node to avoid cross-network latency; for fallbacks we ship a small prefix of KV state to hosted variant — it's eventual consistency; there may be some warmup latency. 06:01 Rina Patel: that's fine as long as we quantify warmup. also curious about tokenization differences across models in case customers mix model families. 06:10 Diego Alvarez: good call. we recommend standardizing tokenizers across a route if exact token accounting and cost are important; otherwise we compute cost at the model-level and normalize in billing. 06:21 Toni Ruiz: are there any pre-reqs for node hardware? our reseller customers vary a lot. 06:26 Diego Alvarez: min spec we recommend is A100/80GB or equivalent for larger models; for quantized LLMs, T4/16GB or RTX6000 may work for small-volume inference. we can provide a hardware compatibility doc. 06:39 Alex Morgan: excellent. there is also a question around software licensing for third-party models — some customers use licensed models — how do you handle that? 06:48 Priya Nair: we can either bring-your-own-weights (BYOW) and run under customer's license, or we can host licensed variants and ensure license compliance through our model catalog controls. 06:58 Samir Banerjee: what about auditability for model access — can we get per-token provenance if required for compliance? 07:05 Diego Alvarez: yes we can emit per-request metadata and logs, including model id, route, user id (if provided), and token counts. retention and export policies are configurable. 07:18 George Ito: ok next let's talk about failure modes — what happens when on-prem node is saturated? 07:23 Maya Chen: routing policy can do immediate fallback to hosted or queue requests until node de-saturates; we recommend fallback to hosted for latency-sensitive flows and queueing for batch jobs. 07:36 Rina Patel: do you support backpressure signals to our ingress gateway? 07:40 Diego Alvarez: yep, our agent exposes a health endpoint and backpressure headers that your gateway can interpret. 07:49 Alex Morgan: question from sales: what's typical onboarding time for an EdgeWay reseller customer? 07:54 Priya Nair: average is 4-6 weeks for small pilots; for larger regulated enterprises that require Private deployment it can be 8-12 weeks including SOC2 questionnaires and network approvals. 08:07 Toni Ruiz: that's acceptable. one of our concerns is reseller support SLAs — can EdgeWay surface Redwood incidents in their portal? 08:15 Maya Chen: we provide an integration API for incidents and metrics — partners can surface it in their portal. for critical customers, Dedicated capacity comes with SLA, and partners can piggyback on that. 08:28 Samir Banerjee: about encryption at rest — does Redwood support customer-managed keys for disk encryption on on-prem nodes? 08:35 Diego Alvarez: yes, on on-prem nodes you manage the encryption keys; for hosted components we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS. 08:45 Alex Morgan: can you give us a sample network diagram and a secure deployment checklist? 08:50 Maya Chen: yes we'll include a runbook, a network diagram, and a checklist in the follow-up email. 08:56 Rina Patel: for the pilot harness, any preferred load generator? we use locust and k6 internally. 09:02 Diego Alvarez: we have an open-source harness based on k6, but can adapt for locust. we'll ship the harness and a docker image. 09:10 George Ito: great. also would like to do a short technical deep-dive after the runbook is digested — maybe a 90m session on kernel selection and quantization profiles. 09:19 Maya Chen: sure, Diego can lead that. 09:22 Alex Morgan: timeline — can we aim to start the pilot week on 2/26? 09:26 Maya Chen: 2/26 start works from our side. we'll prepare the benchmark plan by 2/22. 09:32 Samir Banerjee: security review — please also include our vendor risk questionnaire answers in the thread; we'll need the artifacts to close procurement. 09:39 Maya Chen: will do. I'll attach SOC2/ISO links, and include the KMS/HSM doc. 09:44 Toni Ruiz: commercial — what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated vs pilot? 09:48 Priya Nair: pilot has no long-term commitment; Dedicated is contracted reserved capacity starting monthly, typical minimums vary by region but we'll propose options in pricing. 09:58 Alex Morgan: ok let's run through quick recap and next steps. 10:02 Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to send runbook, network diagram, SOC2/ISO links, and benchmark harness. EdgeWay to upload token mix and QPS spreadsheet. schedule pilot 2/26-3/4. Diego to prepare test plan. Samir will confirm KMS/HSM requirements. any final questions? 10:20 George Ito: none here. 10:22 Alex Morgan: no, thanks, good productive call. 10:24 Maya Chen: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links and calendar invite for pilot kickoff. 10:30 [MISC / NON-SPEECH / LAUGHTER] 10:35 Speaker 3: (inaudible) 10:40 End of recording.
